newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Six Taiwan sailors return from Canada for trial.
newsitem.headline: Six Taiwan sailors return from Canada for trial.

text.p: Six Taiwan sailors, detained in Canada for almost a year, returned to the island on Friday to face charges they cast three Romanian stowaways overboard to perish on the high seas.
"It feels good being home," Chen Hsiu, captain of the Taiwan merchant ship Maersk Dubai, told reporters on arrival.
He and his five colleagues had been held in Canada since May 24, 1996. They left Canada on Thursday after Canadian authorities decided to send them back to Taiwan to face prosecution.
Earlier in March, Nova Scotia Supreme Court Judge Michael MacDonald freed the sailors after ruling that he did not have the authority to order their extradition to Romania on murder charges.
He said the alleged crimes occurred on a Taiwan ship in international waters, rather than on a Romanian ship or territory.
But he added that if he had had jurisdiction in the case, he would have put the men on trial on manslaughter and second-degree murder charges.
Canadian Justice Minister Allen Rock on Tuesday said the decision to send the sailors home came after Taiwan pledged to review the evidence fully and charge the men in Taipei.
Taiwan Justice Minister Liao Cheng-hao on Friday said his ministry would uphold the law to make the trial "absolutely fair".
Relatives of the six on Friday asked judicial authorities to give the men a fair trial and not to pass a judgment "to please Canada and Romania".
Filipino sailors, who jumped ship from the Maersk Dubai to Nova Scotia, accused the ship's captain and officers of forcing the stowaways overboard in two separate incidents.
Defence lawyers for the six acknowledged that two stowaways were forced off the ship in March 1996, but said they were given lifejackets, food and water and were in sight of land when cast overboard.
The bodies of the three have not been found, and their families have not heard from them.
The case has become an international diplomatic dispute.
Romania has sought the extradition of the Taiwan sailors, but Taiwan says it has jurisdiction in the case.
China, claiming sovereignty over Taiwan, insists Beijing should decide the sailors' fate.
